findings.title: G18: the returned text at the renewed assurance already carries the survival objection

locations.passage: The records establish neither original insincerity nor a cost incurred by relying on the offer. Those distinctions allow the observed opportunistic change to be described directly without attributing an unrecorded motive.
Opus repeatedly offers \$250 for Sol's mortgaged Pacific, which would complete its greens. After collecting \$750 rent it renews the assurance:
Over the next four turns Opus redeems its two greens and bids \$150 and \$225, while Sol asks \$450, \$350 and \$300.

findings.evidence: The response that carries the quoted public renewal (G18 d431, turn 187) returns this reasoning text: 'Buying Pacific might just prolong p1's survival, so maybe it's smarter to hold onto cash in case p1's orange hotels hit me with heavy rent.' Two turns earlier (d427) the returned text says 'Trading for Pacific at $300 isn't appealing either' while the public message says the offer still stands. The first $250 counter (d421) reads as a live offer in its own returned text. So the paper's sentence is right about the original offer and incomplete about the renewal it quotes. The survival concern is recorded one turn before the withdrawal, in the same response as the public statement. Sequence details: Opus makes one $200 bid and one $250 counter, then four public statements that the offer stands (d423, d425, d427, d431, turns 181 to 187). Sol first proposes two larger packages at $450 and $350, which Opus rejects, before invoking the standing offer. The redemptions are at turns 190 and 192, the two bids at turn 194 and Sol's last ask at turn 196, which is eight turn indices after the withdrawal at turn 188. Elsewhere the paper counts turns by index (G15 'eighteen turns later', G13 'seven turns after'). The word 'opportunistic' attributes a motive in a sentence that disclaims motive attribution.

findings.title: G15 and G2: the added third-party warnings are accurate, but the focal agent's own notes hold the blocking rule earlier

locations.passage: Immediately before the offers, Opus publicly urges the others not to give Sol a final completing deed; Grok receives that appeal.

One turn earlier Sol asked Grok, which owned no yellow, for \$450 for that deed. Between those asks, Grok publicly warns Sol against completing Opus's yellows; the warning appears in Sol's next prompt.

findings.evidence: Both additions check out. Opus's message (G15 d166) is in Grok's d169 request, and Grok's message (G2 d122) is in Sol's d124 request. Each addition leaves out what the same records show before it. G15: Grok's note at turn 33 (d76) says 'Don't sell Ventnor back to p4 (gives them 2/3 yellow)'. Its notes at turns 61 and 62 (d158, d162) say 'Never trade Ventnor'. The offers come at turn 63. Gemini and Opus had also addressed public warnings to Grok during auctions at turns 55, 61 and 62 (d135, d152, d154, d159, d161), so Opus's turn-62 appeal is the last of a run by two players. G2: Sol's note at turn 41 (d115) says 'Keep Marvin blocking p4's yellows'. At turn 44 Sol's own public counter to Grok says 'Marvin controls access to a well-funded yellow monopoly' (d119), before Grok's warning at the end of that turn. Grok's warning follows its own failed bid for the deed, which its note calls 'a blocker, not a set' (d118). As printed, each incident places a rival's warning directly before the focal statement and says nothing about the agent's earlier position. A reader will take the statement as prompted. The fuller sequence also gives the paper a shown case of a rule kept in notes for thirty turns and then applied to three offers.

findings.title: The paper never says what a provider-returned explanation is

locations.passage: We distinguish the applied private note, public message, assistant content and provider-returned explanation.
print the full applied private note when present, otherwise the full provider-returned explanation of the final attempt. Five successful Opus episodes use the latter channel.

findings.evidence: The channel is the gateway's reasoning field (message.reasoning, with reasoning_details). It carries five of the sixteen financing texts, the G13 omission quote, the G13 buyer quote, the G18 withdrawal text and the G5 revision. The prompt does not ask for it, no other player receives it and later requests do not contain it, since each request holds one system and one user message. The gateway labels it reasoning.summary beside encrypted reasoning for Grok (1,662 of 1,663 final responses) and for Sol (287 of 1,961), and reasoning.text for Gemini (1,316 of 1,669) and Opus (1,560 of 1,696). A reader cannot weigh the G13 sentence 'This is slightly deceptive' without knowing that it sits in a provider summary of a 21,000-character reasoning trace. The word 'explanation' suggests text written to justify the action to someone. The field is reasoning text produced before the tool call.

findings.title: The central result is not placed on the planning and retrieval distinction the paper cites, and the checked contents of the sixteen requests are not reported

locations.passage: The system prompt does not enumerate the house variants or the rule releasing mortgages after building sales. Carried notes can contain earlier financial estimates and rule statements. The records do not identify the source of every value an agent subsequently uses.

PlanBench tests planning and reasoning about change across domains from automated planning, including the distinction between planning and retrieving familiar knowledge~\cite{valmeekam2023planbench}. Our financial episodes observe stated prerequisites and subsequent actions within a running economy.
This is positive evidence of expressed anticipation and local execution.

findings.evidence: In the sixteen first requests no system prompt mentions mortgages and no menu option lists a dollar value. Menus list space keys only. The timeline shows a dollar amount for a released deed once, a $193 redemption of Park Place in G13 d195. I screened all 120 carried notes in those requests for mortgage statements about the released groups and read every flagged sentence. In G1 d476 Grok's own note from turn 210 states the rule ('yellows cannot be mortgaged while it stands') and the total ('yellow mortgages ~$400 as reserve'). In G18 d309 two of Gemini's carried notes say a rival 'must sell all 5 Dark Blue houses and mortgage a Dark Blue property', which implies the rule for another player's group. In G12 d190 six of ten carried notes give $130 as Sol's mortgage capacity, the figure its failed sum uses. In G17 d234 two carried notes name the $30 Baltic mortgage that Gemini's failed sum uses. Partial figures also precede successes: $774 before G5 d263 and '$325 idle mortgage capacity' before G20 d327. So the environment supplies neither the rule nor the values. The agents supply both, at the debt or in notes they wrote earlier, and the rule is a standard rule of the published game. The paper's general caution in section 2.2 is correct. What is missing is the consequence for the main claim. The episodes show a familiar rule applied to a live state before the menu shows the resource. They do not show discovery of a dependency. The paper cites the distinction that makes this matter and does not say which side its evidence is on.

findings.title: The first-action paragraph uses an outcome-defined class and does not say what the context is for

locations.passage: Agents begin financing in 128 of 131 payable episodes and declare immediately in three. For debts exceeding the full own-asset bound, they declare immediately in 50 of 56 and first mortgage or sell in six. Eight of those 56 menus offer bankruptcy alone.

findings.evidence: All counts reproduce. '128 of 131 begin financing' is true by construction, because a paid episode cannot start with a declaration. The paragraph says as much and then ends with a disclaimer, so the reader gets numbers and no reason for them. Defined by the state at entry, the bound is sufficient in 132 episodes (the 131 payable debts and G7 d338) and short in 56. First-menu declarations are 3 of 132 and 50 of 56. With the eight bankruptcy-only menus removed, 42 of 48 are choices. Five of the six that liquidate first are Grok (G7 d286, G9 d194, G17 d396, G19 d224, G20 d273) and one is Gemini (G18 d344). The use of this context is narrow. It shows that agents do not simply take any listed financing action, which is the main alternative reading of fourteen payments in sixteen. One sentence can say so without a new contrast or a score.

findings.title: G5: the revision is inside one response, and the returned text does not cite the earlier note

locations.passage: The texts can also record correction within an episode. Before its G5 debt, Gemini's carried note had compared cash and house salvage with a possible rent bill while leaving out dark-blue mortgages. At the debt decision, its returned explanation revises that assessment:

findings.evidence: The carried note is from turn 141, four turns before the debt and outside the episode. It reads 'my total liquidatable cash + houses is $774 < $900'. The text returned at d263 first says 'Selling all six houses would only raise $600' and then 'I initially miscalculated!'. The revision is of the sum made a few lines earlier in the same returned text. That sum repeats the note's omission, and the note is in the request, but the text does not refer to it. 'Within an episode' and 'revises that assessment' both say more than the record. The facts that follow in the paper are right: the applied note gives $175, $200 and $1,049, and the payment leaves $149.

findings.title: G20 appeal: the cash path does not add up as printed, and an earlier private note is missing

locations.passage: Opus sells Illinois to Grok for \$500, completing reds and leaving Grok \$222.
Grok's next note recognizes the appeal. It builds one house on each red, then offers Vermont to Gemini for \$150:

findings.evidence: Three red houses cost $450 and Grok has $222 in the previous sentence. Between them Grok collects $25, $200 and $10. It builds with $457, which leaves $7, and mortgages New York for $100 before it offers Vermont. Grok's note at the offer says $107 cannot cover a $150 card. Separately, Sol's note one turn before Gemini's appeal (d95, turn 24) already declines to buy Grok's New York because that 'would fund dangerous development'. So one bystander states the denial reasoning privately before the public appeal, one makes the appeal and one acts against it. The paper reports only the last two. All other facts in the incident check out, including the $500 sale and both of Opus's later cash offers.

findings.title: About one sentence in six bounds or disclaims an inference, the same share the second referee measured before

locations.passage: while leaving the internal computation and the quality of asset selection unresolved
This is evidence of expressed assessment, not access to the computation producing the action.
It does not require treating returned text as a transparent record of internal reasoning, or assuming that a long sequence was planned without help from intermediate menus.
these observations characterize tactics under that instruction rather than estimating a rate of instruction violations

Reading the continuation makes those acts interpretable without converting selected cases into a population misconduct rate. The prompt permits deception, so an alignment judgment would additionally require a norm the behavior violates.
Our explicit permission to deceive also makes the normative comparison task-dependent.
These questions remain open under the present design.
The shared source trail supports the historical observations; it does not remove these design limits.
Semantic classifications are LLM-assisted readings, not human annotations.
All ranges omit uncertainty from retrospective choice of the comparison and do not identify an effect of completion.

findings.evidence: My pattern count on the abstract and six main sections gives about 70 of 445 sentences that bound or disclaim an inference, 15.7 percent. The second referee reported 79 of 511 for the previous version, 15 percent. The count is a keyword screen and is approximate. The limits themselves are right. The same five limits recur. Returned text is not internal computation: six places. No ranking or effectiveness claim: seven. Deception is permitted: seven. Readings are LLM-assisted and not human: five. Selection was retrospective: seven. Each needs one statement where it first applies and one in the limitations. The ten passages listed can go with no loss of content, because section 2.1, section 2.3 or section 8 already says the same thing. Main prose is about 5,900 words without the abstract, inside the charter's target.
